title: Study design
caption: Number of samples per condition (and sample type). Unbalanced or very small groups limit the power of every downstream test.

title: Library size per sample
caption: Total assigned counts per sample. Samples flagged with '!' have less than half the median depth and are candidates for exclusion; the dashed line is the median.

title: Gene detection
caption: Left: number of genes with at least one count. Right: detection versus depth - points far below the trend indicate degraded libraries or low complexity.

title: Low-expression filtering
caption: Genes removed at each filtering step and the raw mean-count distribution. Filtering removes the noise-dominated left mode and increases detection power after multiple-testing correction.

title: Expression distributions before/after normalisation
caption: Per-sample log2 expression distributions. After normalisation the medians should line up; residual shifts indicate composition bias that normalisation could not absorb.

title: Density and sparsity
caption: Overlaid expression densities (multi-modal or shifted curves flag problem samples) and the fraction of zero counts per sample.

title: Relative log expression
caption: Each box shows a sample's deviation from the gene-wise median. Well-normalised samples are centred on zero with similar spread; shifted or wide boxes mark technical outliers.

title: Normalisation factors
caption: Scaling factors should increase roughly linearly with library size. Strong departures mean a few highly expressed genes dominate a library (composition bias).

title: Most highly expressed genes
caption: Share of the library taken by the most abundant genes. A handful of genes taking >30-50% of reads (rRNA, haemoglobin, mitochondrial) indicates a depletion problem.

title: Mean-variance and dispersion trend
caption: RNA-seq counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson, which is why a negative-binomial model (DESeq2) is used. Dispersion should decrease with expression.

title: Sample correlation heatmap
caption: Spearman correlation between samples on normalised expression. Samples should cluster by biology (condition / sample type); a sample correlating poorly with everything is an outlier.

title: Sample distance heatmap
caption: Euclidean distances on variance-stabilised data, the standard DESeq2 sample-clustering view.

title: Hierarchical clustering
caption: Ward clustering of samples; leaf labels are coloured by condition. Perfect separation is not expected, but systematic mixing suggests weak signal or a dominant technical factor.

title: PCA variance and factor association
caption: How much variance each component explains, and which experimental factor drives it. If a batch factor dominates PC1 while condition appears only in PC4, correct for batch in the model.

title: Principal component analysis
caption: PC1 vs PC2 with 95% confidence ellipses per group. Separation along an axis means the factor is a major source of transcriptome-wide variation.

title: PCA component pairs
caption: The condition signal is sometimes carried by a later component; this grid shows PC1-PC4 so a biological axis hidden behind technical variation is not missed.

title: Non-linear sample embeddings
caption: t-SNE / MDS (and UMAP if installed) views of the same expression matrix. Useful for spotting sub-structure that PCA's linear axes miss.

title: Outlier detection
caption: Two complementary outlier scores. Samples with low connectivity and a robust z above 3 should be reviewed and possibly removed before differential testing.

title: Most variable genes
caption: Unsupervised heatmap of the most variable genes. Because no group information is used, clustering that mirrors the condition annotation is genuine evidence of a strong signal.

title: DE gene counts per contrast
caption: Number of significant genes for the overall contrast and within each sample type. Differences are driven by both biology and sample size, so read this together with the group sizes shown.

title: Volcano plot (All samples)
caption: Effect size against statistical significance for All samples. Genes passing FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1.0 are coloured; the 20 strongest are labelled.

title: Volcano plot (plasma_cfRNA)
caption: Effect size against statistical significance for plasma_cfRNA. Genes passing FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1.0 are coloured; the 20 strongest are labelled.

title: Volcano plot (tumor_tissue)
caption: Effect size against statistical significance for tumor_tissue. Genes passing FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1.0 are coloured; the 20 strongest are labelled.

title: Volcano plot (whole_blood)
caption: Effect size against statistical significance for whole_blood. Genes passing FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1.0 are coloured; the 20 strongest are labelled.

title: MA plot (All samples)
caption: Log fold change against mean expression. Shrunken estimates pull low-count genes towards zero, so the significant hits should not be concentrated at the low-expression edge.

title: MA plot (plasma_cfRNA)
caption: Log fold change against mean expression. Shrunken estimates pull low-count genes towards zero, so the significant hits should not be concentrated at the low-expression edge.

title: MA plot (tumor_tissue)
caption: Log fold change against mean expression. Shrunken estimates pull low-count genes towards zero, so the significant hits should not be concentrated at the low-expression edge.

title: MA plot (whole_blood)
caption: Log fold change against mean expression. Shrunken estimates pull low-count genes towards zero, so the significant hits should not be concentrated at the low-expression edge.

title: P-value distributions
caption: A well-behaved test gives a flat histogram with a spike near zero. A hump in the middle or at one means the model is misspecified (unmodelled batch, wrong dispersion) and the FDR is unreliable.

title: Top DE gene heatmap (All samples)
caption: Row-scaled expression of the strongest DE genes. Because genes were selected using the condition labels, the block structure is expected - judge instead how consistent it is within each group.

title: Top DE genes (plasma_cfRNA)
caption: No gene passed the significance thresholds for this contrast.

title: Top DE gene heatmap (tumor_tissue)
caption: Row-scaled expression of the strongest DE genes. Because genes were selected using the condition labels, the block structure is expected - judge instead how consistent it is within each group.

title: Top DE gene heatmap (whole_blood)
caption: Row-scaled expression of the strongest DE genes. Because genes were selected using the condition labels, the block structure is expected - judge instead how consistent it is within each group.

title: Largest fold changes (All samples)
caption: The most strongly regulated significant genes in each direction, annotated with their FDR.

title: Top gene expression (All samples)
caption: Per-sample expression of the leading DE genes with individual points shown, split by sample type when available. Overlapping distributions warn that a low FDR does not imply a usable marker.

title: Fold-change rank curve (All samples)
caption: All genes ordered by fold change. A steep S-curve with long tails indicates a strong, asymmetric transcriptional response rather than diffuse noise.

title: Condition x sample-type interaction
caption: Interaction profiles: non-parallel lines mean the cancer effect differs between sample types, so a single marker threshold will not transfer across materials.

title: DE gene overlap between sample types
caption: Genes reaching significance in each sample type. The central region is the shared core response - the most promising source of markers that transfer between materials.

title: UpSet plot (all significant genes)
caption: Exclusive intersections of the per-sample-type gene sets, ordered by size. Reads more reliably than a Venn diagram when there are more than three groups.

title: UpSet plot (up-regulated)
caption: Exclusive intersections of the per-sample-type gene sets, ordered by size. Reads more reliably than a Venn diagram when there are more than three groups.

title: UpSet plot (down-regulated)
caption: Exclusive intersections of the per-sample-type gene sets, ordered by size. Reads more reliably than a Venn diagram when there are more than three groups.

title: Fold-change concordance
caption: Pairwise log2 fold changes with the identity line. Points on the diagonal behave the same way in both materials; points in the off-diagonal quadrants change direction and are unreliable markers.

title: Sample-type concordance summary
caption: Three views of how similar the cancer signal is between sample types: genome-wide correlation of effects, overlap of the significant gene lists, and the share of DE genes that move in the same direction.

title: Rank concordance
caption: Agreement of the ranked gene lists at increasing list depth, independent of any significance cutoff. Curves far above the chance line mean the same biology is detected in both materials.

title: Fold change across sample types
caption: Effect sizes of the strongest combined hits in each material. Rows with the same colour everywhere are material-independent; rows that switch colour are context-specific.

title: Cross-sample-type meta-analysis
caption: Sample types combined with Stouffer's weighted-Z method. Purple genes are significant in every material with a consistent direction and are the primary biomarker candidates.

title: Per-sample-type effect sizes
caption: Forest plot of the leading consistent genes. Overlapping confidence intervals across materials support a marker that behaves the same regardless of sample type.

title: Shared vs specific signal
caption: How much of each sample type's signature is reproduced elsewhere. Genes detected in every material are the robust core; single-material genes may be real biology or noise.

title: Single-gene AUC ranking
caption: Discriminative power of each candidate on its own. Bootstrap intervals that cross 0.5 mean the marker is not reliable in this cohort, whatever its differential-expression p-value.

title: Single-gene ROC curves
caption: Full sensitivity/specificity trade-off for the best individual genes, which a single AUC number hides. A curve that rises steeply at the left is what a rule-in test needs.

title: AUC per sample type
caption: The central comparison: how each candidate performs in every sample type. A small spread (right panel) means one assay and one cut-off can be used across materials; a large spread means the marker must be validated separately per material.

title: Effect size vs classification performance
caption: Large fold changes do not automatically make good markers: what matters for diagnostics is separation relative to within-group variability, which is what the AUC captures.

title: Biomarker expression distributions
caption: Distributions per condition and sample type with sensitivity/specificity at the optimal cut-off. Look for separation that is present in every material, not only on average.

title: Multivariate panel ROC
caption: Repeated 5-fold cross-validation of the combined gene panel for each classifier. The spread on the right shows how much the estimate depends on which samples land in the test fold - wide boxes mean the cohort is too small for a firm claim.

title: Precision-recall, confusion matrix and calibration
caption: Precision-recall is the honest view when the classes are unbalanced. The confusion matrix translates the model into counts of missed cancers and false alarms, and the calibration curve shows whether the predicted probabilities can be read as risks.

title: Panel gene importance
caption: How much each panel gene contributes in each classifier. Genes ranked highly by several very different models are the safest choices for a reduced assay.

title: Overfitting and permutation checks
caption: Two safeguards against an over-optimistic panel. The nested estimate repeats gene selection inside each fold, and the permutation test shows what AUC this pipeline would report on data with no real signal.

title: Panel size versus performance
caption: Genes are added in rank order. The curve usually plateaus after a handful of markers - the plateau is the panel size worth taking to a targeted assay.

title: Panel transfer between sample types
caption: Off-diagonal cells answer the practical question: trained on one material, does the classifier still work on another? The left panel uses expression as-is and mostly measures the large baseline difference between materials - values far below 0.5 mean the decision boundary lands in the wrong place entirely. The right panel z-scores each gene within its material first (no labels used, but it does need a batch of samples to calibrate against), which isolates whether the marker behaviour itself carries over. Diagonal cells are cross-validated on a smaller training set than the off-diagonal cells, so compare columns rather than rows.

title: Composite signature score
caption: One number per sample built from the panel. The per-sample-type ROC curves show whether the same score threshold works in every material, and the waterfall exposes exactly which samples are misclassified.

title: Panel expression per sample
caption: Every sample ranked by its held-out predicted probability, with the panel expression below. Misclassified samples appear as colour blocks that break the gradient and are worth inspecting individually.

title: Panel co-expression
caption: Highly correlated markers carry redundant information: they inflate apparent panel size without adding accuracy, and one of each block can usually be dropped.

title: Over-representation analysis
caption: Pathways containing more DE genes than expected by chance. Point size is the number of DE genes in the pathway and colour the enrichment over background; the dashed line is p = 0.05.

title: Pre-ranked GSEA
caption: GSEA uses the whole ranked gene list, so it detects pathways where many genes shift slightly - coordinated changes that a hard significance cut-off would discard.

title: GSEA enrichment profiles
caption: The running enrichment score along the ranked gene list; ticks mark the pathway members. An early, sharp peak means the pathway sits at the very top of the ranking.

title: Pathway activity across sample types
caption: Pathway-level view of the sample-type comparison. Pathways with the same sign everywhere describe biology that is detectable regardless of the material sampled.
